abstract: The Wharton AI & Analytics Initiative and Accenture developed the Wharton-Accenture Skills Index (WAsX), an empirical benchmark tracking more than 150 million unique U.S. profiles and 100 million job postings. The report finds a structural skills mismatch: workers oversupply generalist traits while employers increasingly demand specialized, execution-oriented skills. AI is accelerating this divergence by redistributing economic value from routine cognitive tasks toward judgment, coordination, and specialized knowledge.
keyFindings: WAsX tracks 150 million+ unique U.S. profiles and 100 million+ job postings to measure talent market evolution
Workers oversupply broad generalist traits (communication, leadership, problem-solving) while employers reward specialized, role-dependent skills
AI is redistributing economic value away from routine cognitive tasks toward judgment, coordination, and specialized knowledge
Skill value is not universal: some skills raise wages in one role but reduce them in another
Generative AI has been described as 'a positively destructive bomb on roles and titles' by making workers able to carry out tasks they previously could not
methodology: Empirical analysis of 150M+ unique U.S. worker profiles and 100M+ job postings. Accenture's Generative AI exposure metric was applied from O*NET tasks to roles, with skill clusters assigned GenAI exposure terciles. Job posting demand trends analyzed from 2022 onward.
qualifiers: The study found no massive wage swings tied to individual skills. The authors note that employers, workers, and universities continue to operate in a role-based world while the economy has shifted to a skills-based system. Specific wage premium figures were not reported in available summaries.
